title: Read a graph as a story

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A graph over time tells a story, read from left to right.

do.text: A graph over time tells a story

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: This tub holds water. Time runs across the graph, and the water level runs up.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The gold point's height is always the water level.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Turn on the tap. As time passes, the water rises, and the point climbs with it.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The water level is increasing: it is getting higher.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The rate is how fast the level changes. Each equal step of time adds the same rise, so this rate is steady.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Turn the tap off. Time keeps passing, so the point moves right, but the level holds.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The level is constant: it stays the same.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Pull the plug. The level is decreasing: it is getting lower.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Filling took this long; draining took much less time for the same change in height.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: So draining was faster, and its piece is steeper.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Now empty the tub and fill it again, opening the tap wider and wider.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The level rises faster and faster, so the graph bends upward.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Take two equal steps of time: the first gives a small rise, the second a much bigger one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A steady rate draws a straight line: linear.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A changing rate draws a curve: nonlinear.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A drone climbs, then descends, then climbs. Which description fits the graph of the height above the ground over time, read from left to right?

do.text: A drone climbs, then descends, then climbs. Which description fits the graph of the height above the ground over time, read from left to right?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Climbs: the height is increasing.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Descends: it is decreasing.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Climbs again: increasing.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Increasing, then decreasing, then increasing.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: x, minutes; y, meters from home. From A to B, how does y change?

do.text: $x$: minutes; $y$: meters from home. From $A$ to $B$, how does $y$ change?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A common slip reads the falling line as walking downhill.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: But the graph is not a picture of the path. Its height is the traveler's distance from home: five meters at A.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: From A to B, the height falls to three: the traveler gets closer to home.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The distance from home decreases.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A level piece would mean the distance stays the same, usually because the traveler stopped.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Up is increasing, level is constant, and down is decreasing.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Straight is a steady rate; curved, a changing rate.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Read left to right. The height is how much; the steepness is how fast.
